best_for: Developers leaving Docker Desktop, or new to containers, who want a free GUI for Podman, Compose and local Kubernetes clusters on Windows, Mac or Linux.

points.title: Free and open source, no license tiers
points.text: Podman Desktop is Apache-2.0 licensed and free for any use, including at work. It is a CNCF project; Red Hat offers a separate build with paid enterprise support.

points.title: Containers and Kubernetes in one window
points.text: Build, pull and push images, start containers, read logs and open a terminal. It runs Compose files and can create local Kind or Minikube clusters or connect to existing ones, then apply YAML and forward ports.

points.title: Docker habits carry over
points.text: The docs cover importing saved containers, aliasing the `docker` command and using `DOCKER_HOST`, so most scripts keep working. Podman runs containers without a daemon and can run them rootless.

points.title: On Windows it needs a Linux VM
points.text: Podman runs inside a Linux machine on WSL 2 or Hyper-V. Turning on either feature needs administrator rights, and the docs ask for 6 GB of RAM for that machine. The installer listed here is per-machine, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: On Mac, use the .dmg
points.text: The project recommends its .dmg because it bundles the Podman engine and avoids path problems seen with package managers. Builds exist for Intel and Apple silicon, and macOS 13 or later is required.

points.title: Extensions and a local AI lab
points.text: Extensions add features, and Podman AI Lab can download models and start a local inference server. GPU acceleration is supported for those workloads.

points.title: Flatpak and older versions
points.text: The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as Red Hat's own, for x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 63 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
